182:
(a) A manufacturer of wine must follow certain distance requirements from churches, schools, housing authorities, alcoholic treatment centers and other specific locations as required by section 4-38 of this chapter.
(b) All measurements to determine distances required by this chapter shall be measured as provided for in section 4-38.
(c) A winery is located on premises, a substantial portion of which is used for agricultural purposes, including the cultivation of grapes, berries, or fruits to be utilized in the manufacture or production of wine by the winery; or owned and operated by persons who are engaged in the production of a substantial portion of the agricultural produce used in its annual production.
(d) The license required to be obtained by a manufacturer of wine shall include the right to offer wine samples and to make retail sales of its wine and the wine of any other Georgia farm winery in a tasting room on the premises of the winery, or on property located contiguous to the farm winery and owned by the farm winery, in closed packages for consumption off the premises.
(1) "Tasting room" means an outlet for the promotion of a farm winery's wine by providing samples of such wine to the public and for the sale of such wine at retail in closed packages for consumption off the premises. Samples of wine can be given free of charge or for a fee.
(2) A winery's wine may also be sold offsite in a special entertainment district designated by the city council.
(e) Any Georgia farm winery may be authorized to sell up to twenty-four thousand (24,000) gallons per calendar year of its wine at wholesale within the state; provided, however, that a licensed farm winery shall not be authorized to sell its wine at wholesale unless such licensed farm winery shall have first offered its products for sale at a fair market wholesale price to a licensed Georgia wholesaler and such wholesaler does not accept the farm winery's product within thirty (30) days of such offer.
(f) A farm winery licensee shall also be authorized to sell, deliver, or ship its wine in bulk or in bottles, whether labeled or unlabeled, in accordance with regulations of the state, to Georgia farm winery licensees and shall be authorized to acquire and receive deliveries and shipments of such wine made by Georgia farm winery licensees.
(g) Wines sold at retail by a manufacturer as provided in this Code section shall have levied thereon an excise tax as prescribed by section 4-176.
(h) A Georgia farm winery licensee shall be authorized, in accordance with regulations of the state, to acquire and receive deliveries and shipments of wine in bulk from out-of-state producers and shippers in an amount not to exceed forty (40) percent of its annual production.
(i) Any wine received in bulk pursuant to paragraph (h) of this subsection shall have levied thereon the requisite taxes as prescribed by section 4-176, and such taxes shall be reported and remitted to the city.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
185:
(a) A retail dealer of malt beverages and wine by the package must follow certain distance requirements for package sales from churches, schools, housing authorities, alcoholic treatment centers and other specific locations as required by section 4-38 of this chapter.
(b) All measurements to determine distances required by this chapter shall be measured as provided for in section 4-38.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
186:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage on the premises licensed for the sale of malt beverages or wine by the package, and it shall be unlawful for any licensee by the package to open for, or break the package for, a purchaser and/or permit the consumption of alcoholic beverages on said premises.
(b) This section shall not apply to the following:
(1) For the holder of a temporary limited license as provided for in this chapter during the hours for which the temporary limited license is valid.
(2) Samples of tap malt beverages or wine that may be made available to growler purchasers.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
187:
(a) Package malt beverage licensees or wine licensees, who are not also licensed to sell distilled spirits by the package, may fill growlers with malt beverages and/or wine at the licensed location subject to the following requirements:
(1) At least ninety (90) percent of the licensee's total gross sales are from packaged sale of malt beverages and/or wine or the licensee's premises has a minimum of four hundred (400) square feet of floor space dedicated to the display of malt beverages and/or wine offered for sale.
(2) A growler shall not exceed sixty-four (64) ounces. Growlers may only be filled from kegs or barrels procured by the licensee from a duly licensed wholesaler.
(3) Only professionally sanitized and sealed growlers may be filled and made available for retail sale.
(4) Each growler must be securely sealed and removed from the premises in its original sealed condition.
(5) Consumption on the premises from the growler is prohibited, however, samples of tap malt beverages or wine may be made available but shall not exceed more than a total of twenty-four (24) ounces which shall be comprised of at least four (4) different varieties of malt beverages or wine.
(6) A licensee may charge a fee for samples of tap malt beverages or wine.
(7) The filling of growlers by means of a tapped keg shall not constitute the breaking of the package.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
190:
(a) A retail dealer in consumption on the premises of malt beverages and wine must follow certain distance requirements for package and consumption sales from churches, schools, housing authorities, alcoholic treatment centers and other specific locations as required by section 4-38 of this chapter.
(b) All measurements to determine distances required by this chapter shall be measured as provided for in section 4-38.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
191:
(a) A consumption on premises licensee shall not permit a purchaser to remove from the premises any alcoholic beverage, and it is the licensee's responsibility to ensure that no beverages are sold and carried out.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any licensee hereunder to make deliveries of any alcoholic beverage beyond the boundaries of the premises covered by the license.
(c) It is prohibited for customers to gather outside an alcoholic beverage premises and consume alcoholic beverages.
(d) It is prohibited for the manager or any employee to allow persons to gather outside an alcoholic beverage premises and consume alcoholic beverages.
(e) This section shall not apply in the following instances:
(1) For special alcohol events that are sponsored, organized, or approved by the City of Cairo, and where the alcohol is obtained from a participating business within a designated area and is contained in and consumed from an approved, plastic cup and where the person consuming or possessing such alcohol is wearing an approved wristband or armband provided by the licensed alcohol dealer.
(2) Where the city council through a resolution has permitted otherwise.
(3) For restaurants that have a valid open air, patio, or sidewalk cafe permit provided that all outdoor activities are contained within the permitted cafe.
(4) Beverages for consumption at a publicly owned or privately owned golf course.
(5) For the carrying out of a partially consumed bottle of wine as defined in section 4-92.
(6) For pool and patio areas of hotels licensed for on-premises consumption.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19; Ord. No. 842, § 2, 7-11-22)
192:
(a) Any restaurant which is licensed to sell wine for consumption on the premises may permit a patron to remove one (1) unsealed bottle of wine per patron for consumption off premises, if the patron has purchased a meal and consumed a portion of the bottle of wine which has been purchased with such meal on the restaurant's premises.
(b) A partially consumed bottle of wine that is to be removed from the premises must be securely resealed by the licensee or its employees before removal from the premises.
(c) The partially consumed bottle of wine shall be placed in a bag or other container that is secured in such a manner that it is visibly apparent if the container has been subsequently opened or tampered with, and a dated receipt for the bottle of wine and meal shall be provided by the licensee and attached to the container.
(d) If transporting in a motor vehicle, the container with the resealed bottle of wine shall be placed in a locked glove compartment, a locked trunk, or the area behind the last upright seat of a motor vehicle that is not equipped with a trunk.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
195:
(a) A retail dealer in the sale of distilled spirits by the package must follow certain distance requirements for package and consumption sales from churches, schools, housing authorities, alcoholic treatment centers and other specific locations as required by section 4-38 of this chapter.
(b) All measurements to determine distances required by this chapter shall be measured as provided for in section 4-38.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
197:
(a) No display of advertisement or information regarding prices of distilled spirits will be allowed in any show window or other place visible from outside the licensee's place of business.
(1) Except as otherwise provided in subsection (2) of this section, a licensed retail dealer in packaged distilled spirits may display at the licensee's place of business unilluminated signs, using letters not larger than eight (8) inches in height, flat against the outside of the building, below the roofline, bearing the words "liquor," "beer," "wine," "champagne," or any combination thereof, and "package store" or "liquor store," together with the trade name of the retail dealer. In addition to such signs flat against the outside of the building, the retail dealer may display at a location on the tract of property upon which the business is located, but not affixed to the building, one (1) unilluminated sign using letters not larger than eight (8) inches in height bearing the words "package store" or "liquor store," and the trade name of the retail dealer. A sign not affixed to the building may be no larger than sixteen (16) square feet in area. The trade name of the retailer as listed in the application form submitted to the city clerk in compliance with this section must be considered and found acceptable by the council.
(2) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1) of this section, licensed retail dealers in package distilled spirits may display signs inside and outside their retail establishments which advertise or promote any lottery authorized by the "Georgia Lottery for Education Act."
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
198:
It shall be unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage on the premises licensed for the sale of distilled spirits by the package, and it shall be unlawful for any licensee by the package to open for, or break the package for, a purchaser and/or permit the consumption of alcoholic beverages on said premises.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
199:
The building in which each retail dealer of distilled spirits in the unbroken package is located shall contain sufficient lighting so that the building itself, the premises and all entrances are readily visible at all times from the street on which the building is located so as to reveal the inside retail area of the building and so as to reveal all of the outside premises of such building.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
200:
(a) It shall be permissible for a package dealer in distilled spirits to have a drive-in window, and for the dealer, or an employee, to deliver distilled spirits through that window.

(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)

205:
A person licensed to sell distilled spirits for on-premises consumption shall be authorized to serve malt beverages and wine, after obtaining the appropriate licenses, during the same hours as are permitted under this chapter for the serving of distilled spirits by the drink.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
208:
(a) A distiller in the manufacture of distilled spirits and fortified wines must follow certain distance requirements from churches, schools, housing authorities, alcoholic treatment centers and other specific locations as required by section 4-38 of this chapter.
(b) All measurements to determine distances required by this chapter shall be measured as provided for in section 4-38.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
209:
(a) No individual shall be permitted to own or operate a distillery without first obtaining a proper license from the city.
(b) Distilleries are allowed to act in three (3) distinct capacities. In addition to manufacturing, a distillery can sell its up to five hundred (500) barrels per year of its product to patrons on the premises for consumption on the premises, and/or by the package for consumption off the premises in accordance with state law.
(c) A distiller licensee shall pay all local license fees and excise taxes applicable to individuals licensed under this Code as manufacturers. Such excise taxes shall be paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in distilled spirits; provided, however, taxes shall be imposed upon and paid by the distiller for distilled spirits served or sold by the distiller directly to the public in an on-premises restaurant. A manufacturer is not required to obtain a separate local consumption license. Instead, the city may be able to charge a regulatory fee upon distillers if the city "customarily performs investigation or inspection of such businesses" as a protection of the public health, safety, or welfare related to the requirement that the distiller abide by the days and times of sale.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
210:
A manufacturer of distilled spirits license may also be issued to a fruit grower licensed as a farm winery authorizing such fruit grower to manufacture distilled spirits and fortified wine for sale exclusively through a licensed and designated wholesaler; provided, however, that the farm winery has no more than one (1) tasting room located on its licensed premises. A manufacturer of distilled spirits license may also be issued for the manufacture of distilled spirits from agricultural products other than perishable fruits.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
213:
(a) The city council shall define and designate specific special event area(s) where alcoholic beverages are allowed to be sold and consumed in the open air after a special event permit has been acquired as required by section 4-160 of this Code. These special event areas where alcohol is consumed outdoors shall be conspicuously marked by posted signs at all times at each point of entrance and exit stating the following: "The possession of alcoholic beverages beyond this point is prohibited."
(b) The boundaries of a specific event area(s) shall be defined and shown on a map, which, along with all notations, references, and explanatory matter thereon, are hereby adopted by reference and declared to be a part of, on the date of adoption, of this ordinance [from which this article derives]. Designated event areas may be changed, amended, or deleted by the council at its discretion.
(1) Area No. 1 is to be known as the "Downtown Special Entertainment District"; its boundaries shall be defined as follows:
a. An area beginning at the intersection of South Broad Street and the railroad tracks, then east along the railroad tracks to a point in line with the east right-of-way margin of 1st St., SE, then south along said eastern margin of 1st St., SE to its intersection with 2nd Ave., SE, then west long the north right-of-way of 2nd Ave., SE, continuing across South Broad Street onto the north right-of-way of M. L. King, Jr. Ave., SW, then west along that right-of-way to its intersection with the western right-of-way margin of 1st St., SW, then north along 1st St., SW, crossing over 1st Ave., SW, and continuing north in a line to the railroad tracks, then east to the point of beginning. The area encompassed by these boundaries make up this district.
(2) Area No. 2 is to be known as the "Grady Cultural Center Entertainment District" owned by the City of Cairo, located at 101 First St., NW, and is made up of the area located within its property boundaries.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
214:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by a licensed consumption on premises establishment in a patio/open area type environment if the establishment has been approved as provided in this section.
(b) The requirements for approval are:
(1) The patio/open area must be enclosed by some structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main licensed premises. The only exception to this would be a fire exit as required by building and fire codes. Such fire exit would not be for general public use unless an emergency exists and would be of the type which sounds an alarm so that the establishment would be alerted of unauthorized use if no emergency exists. The height of such structure shall be a minimum of three and one-half (3.5) feet above the patio floor. The structure is not required to be solid nor does it have to restrict visibility into or out of the patio/open area. The patio/open area shall meet all setback requirements as set forth in this Code.
(2) The patio/open area shall not be required to be covered by a roof.
(3) The patio/open area, shall be used merely as an extension of the interior seating area. Service in the patio/open area shall be only by waiter or waitress or by customer self-service at the selling location; i.e., no outside bar or service window.
(c) It is prohibited for an establishment to be in violation of the city's noise ordinance as defined in chapter 12 of the Code of Ordinances and to allow any noise to be created in a patio/open area which may be heard from a distance of one hundred (100) feet from the patio/open area. Any measurement made pursuant to this section shall describe the shortest straight line distance from the patio to the point in question.
(d) Patio/open area plans must be reviewed and approved on an individual basis by the chief of police. Patio/open areas must be permitted and approved by the city's building inspection and fire departments as required by their governing regulations or codes.
(e) Nothing contained herein shall prohibit a hotel or motel with a consumption on the premises license from making sales and allowing consumption of alcoholic beverages in the patio areas of such hotel or motel. "Patio areas," as the term is used herein, do not have to conform to the standards in this section.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
215:
(a) Sidewalk cafes shall be operated by qualified restaurants on public sidewalks and regulated by the City of Cairo to protect the public health, safety, welfare, and the interest of the city and the primary use of the sidewalks by pedestrian traffic.
(1) The use of sidewalks for restaurant tables shall only be permitted incidental to the operation of a "restaurant", and the use of the sidewalk to operate a sidewalk cafe is a privilege, not a right, and any person who violates the conditions of this section may be forbidden to operate a sidewalk cafe after notice and a hearing as per section 4-17.
(2) Sidewalk cafes may be ordered closed temporarily by the City of Cairo whenever deemed necessary in the sole discretion of the city, whenever the area may be needed for a public purpose, including but not limited to construction, maintenance, public health, safety or welfare, emergencies, and public events such as parades or street parties.
(3) The city may order the immediate removal or relocation of all, or parts of, a sidewalk cafe in emergency situations or for safety consideration, without notice. The city and its officers and employees shall not be responsible for sidewalk cafe fixtures relocated during emergencies.
(4) In no event shall the uses permitted in this section reduce that portion of any sidewalk customarily used by pedestrians to less than five (5) feet in width. Additionally, contiguous pedestrian flow must be maintained between two (2) or more adjacent sidewalk cafes. The city may designate portions of the sidewalk which must not be obstructed under any circumstances, and may restrict usage in any manner deemed necessary by the city.
(5) Only the area in front of a restaurant, as defined by projecting its interior width outward perpendicular to the street to a point at which it intersects the roadway (or within the sidewalk frontage of the building where the licensed restaurant is located) can be used by the restaurant.
(6) Nothing will be placed within five (5) feet of a fire hydrant, pedestrian crosswalk, or handicapped corner curb cut.
(7) Sidewalk cafe operators shall maintain the sidewalk and the curb and gutter immediately adjacent to it in a clean and safe condition. Refuse shall not be disposed of in the city's sidewalk trash receptacles.
(8) No tables, chairs, or other parts of sidewalk cafes shall be attached, chained or in any manner affixed to any tree, post, sign, or other fixture, curb, or sidewalk in or near the permitted area. All tables and chairs must be of a design, material, and specification suitable for outside dining.
(b) Only a properly licensed restaurant with a sidewalk cafe, which holds a valid alcohol license for consumption on the premises, may serve alcohol to customers in the sidewalk cafe, subject to the following restrictions:
(1) Alcohol may only be possessed in the interior portion or the sidewalk cafe portion of the restaurant during the times as allowed for consumption of alcoholic beverages on premises.
(2) Alcohol may not be served in its original container, but must be served in clear plastic cups. No bottles, glass, or cans are allowed.
(3) Only a single serving of alcohol may be in possession of any patron.
(4) Patrons must be seated while consuming an alcoholic beverage.
(5) Service in the sidewalk cafe area shall be only by waiter or waitress or by customer self-service at the selling location; i.e., no outside bar or service window.
(6) Smoking is prohibited at tables included in a sidewalk table plan permit area and within five (5) feet of any such area boundary.
(7) Within the designated area of a sidewalk cafe, the operator holding a permit under this section shall have the right to limit access and occupancy to only bona fide paying customers of the operator's restaurant who are behaving in a lawful manner.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
216:
(a) Private clubs, meeting the definition of this chapter, are eligible to apply for a license for consumption on premises of alcoholic beverages.
(b) No license shall be issued or renewed for the sale of alcoholic beverages prior to the furnishing of evidence, satisfactory to the city, that such private club has been approved as a tax exempt entity by the IRS.
(c) A license issued under this subsection shall authorize the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption only on the premises where sold.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
217:
(a) As used in this subsection, the term "drink" means a single portion beverage which contains any alcoholic beverage.
(b) This section shall be construed to cover, include and apply to all alcoholic beverages including malt beverages, wine, and distilled spirits for consumption on premises by properly licensed establishments in the city. All on-premises licensees are prohibited from selling or giving away alcoholic beverages under the following circumstances:
(1) Offering all you can drink for a set price during a set time.
(2) Serving multiple drinks for a single price unless the drinks are part of a variety sampler of which no more than a total of sixteen (16) ounces can be served as part of the sampler and which sampler shall be comprised of at least four (4) different varieties of malt beverages or wine or three (3) different mixes containing distilled spirits.
(3) Making a single price the basis for a required purchase of two (2) or more servings.
(4) Serving alcoholic beverages by the pitcher, except to two (2) or more persons at any one (1) time.
(5) Offering reduced-price drinks to any segment of the population for any period of time as an inducement to patronize the premises; except between the hours of 5:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday, drinks may be sold at a reduced price which is no less than half the price usually charged.
(6) Selling alcoholic beverages for less than half the normal retail price, or selling alcoholic beverages in pitchers or in jumbo sizes for less than half the normal retail price. Nothing contained in this subsection shall be construed to prohibit the dispensing of drinks in pitchers or in jumbo sizes, provided that such pitchers or jumbo sizes shall be available at all times that the licensee is open for business.
(7) Using coupons or other special promotional items as an inducement to purchase alcoholic beverages.
(8) Sponsoring, conducting or allowing contests or other promotions which have as their primary purpose increasing the consumption of alcoholic beverages.
(9) Offering or delivering any free alcoholic beverage to the general public.
(c) The prohibitions and restrictions in the foregoing subsection which apply to licensees or agents or employees of licensees shall not:
(1) Apply at private functions;
(2) Prohibit offering of free food or entertainment at any time;
(3) Prohibit including drinks as part of the price of a hotel, travel, entertainment, or meal package;
(4) Prohibit the sale or offer to sell, wine or malt beverage by the bottle, pitcher, or carafe;
(5) Prohibit any motel or hotel from offering room service to registered guests.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
218:
(a) Non-profit organizations meeting the criteria of subsection (b) below may obtain a consumption on premises license subject to the following conditions that the sale of alcoholic beverages on the premises shall be clearly incidental to the primary function of the non-profit organization.
(b) To qualify for a consumption on premises license, the nonprofit organization must be exempt from federal income taxes pursuant to section 501(c), (d) or (e) of the Internal Revenue Code and must have a building, facility or grounds that is primarily used for public education, research, conservation and enjoyment, or that serves as a repository for a collection of literary, natural, or scientific objects of interest, or works of art where such facility or building is arranged, intended, designed and open to be viewed by members of the public with or without an admission fee. This shall include, but not limited to, a non-profit historical museum.
(c) Non-profit organizations shall be subject to all sections of this chapter, and shall comply with all other applicable state and local license requirements, and may sell on all days and at all times that sales by retailers are lawful within the city.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
219:
(a) The sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises of the Grady Cultural Center, the Zebulon Theatre, and the Grady County Museum and History Center shall be allowed at city approved events.
(b) The downtown development authority, after obtaining the proper license or permit, is allowed to sell alcohol by the drink at the Grady Cultural Center at events approved by the city. The director(s) of the Grady Cultural Center, the Zebulon Theater, or the Grady County Museum and History Center, or their designee(s), may hold an alcoholic beverage license for these locations. There shall be no alcoholic beverage license or permit fees paid to the city by the downtown development authority, the Grady Cultural Center, the Zebulon Theater, or the Grady County Museum and History Center, or their designee(s), but a license or permit may be issued which must be displayed on the premises. If no license is obtained for these non-profit organizations, alcohol event permits may be considered for special temporary events held, if applicable, and may also be catered by a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer.
(c) The consumption on the premises license provided for herein is exempted from the food sale requirements provided for in section 4-7(b)(4) of this chapter.
(d) The hours for sale of alcoholic beverages on the premises of either of these organizations shall be the same as provided in section 4-37 of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
222:
(a) Alcohol event permits may be issued by the City of Cairo for special events that are considered to be of a community nature, and that are advertised and open to the entire community, for the length of the event not to exceed one (1) day.
(b) All alcohol event permits applications are required to be filed at least thirty (30) days prior to the event.
(1) Any alcohol permit that is issued to a non-profit event applicant must hold a valid license which authorize the licensee to sell alcohol for consumption on the premises, or by the package for consumption off the premises, may be issued an off-premises license which authorizes such licensed alcoholic beverage non-profit applicant to sell alcohol by the drink off-premises and connection with an authorized non-profit function.
a. If a group or individual has a fund-raising event where an admission fee is charged and alcoholic beverages are provided, then a special event permit is required. All alcoholic beverages for the event must be acquired from a wholesale distributor or provided by a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer. However, if a group or individual gathering has an event such as a wedding or any gathering where alcohol is provided to guests with no expectation of payment, then a special event permit would not be required. In this case, the alcohol must be obtained from a Georgia licensed retailer of alcoholic beverages.
(2) Holders of a special temporary alcohol event permit shall be considered the same as any other licensee and subject to all laws, rules and regulations and other applicable sections of this chapter relating thereto. Entities selling, and persons consuming, alcoholic beverages under this section shall obey all state laws and city ordinances.
(3) No more than four (4) temporary alcohol permits may be issued to a non-profit organization in any one (1) calendar year pursuant to this section.
(4) Except as provided in this paragraph, manufacturers, brokers, importers, shippers, wholesalers, and retailers shall not make any donations of alcoholic beverages to any non-profit charitable or civic organization except where:
a. A non-profit charitable or civic organization has obtained a special event permit, wholesalers shall be authorized to make donations of alcoholic beverages, provided that the alcoholic beverages were obtained through proper distribution channels and all applicable taxes have been paid.
b. A non-profit charitable or civic organization has been issued a temporary special use permit authorizing the organization to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises or to sell or auction wine only in unbroken packages for consumption off premises. Unlicensed individuals, licensed retailers, and licensed wholesalers shall be authorized to make donations of alcoholic beverages to such organizations, provided that the alcoholic beverages were obtained through proper distribution channels and all applicable taxes have been paid or will be paid. The organization holding the temporary special use permit may ship or otherwise transport donated wine to the location specified in the permit.
c. The amount of such donations shall not exceed the amount necessary for the event for which a special event permit has been obtained.
(5) At the request of a non-profit charitable or civic organization that holds a special event permit, manufacturers, brokers, importers, shippers, or wholesalers may donate services to the organization by having permitted representatives provide pouring services and product information during the event.
(6) Nothing shall prohibit cash donations to charitable and civic organizations provided that such a donation is unconditional and not related to the purchase of a particular brand or brand label of alcoholic beverage.
(7) Permits issued pursuant to this section shall be valid only for the place specified in the permit and are issued under the terms and conditions as determined by the city council and may include notification requirements, security, sanitation, clean-up, beginning and ending dates and times, and more. The permit issued by the city shall not be effective until such time as a permit has been obtained from the state.
(8) Permittees may hold such events on the premises of a licensed manufacturer or wholesaler provided that all alcoholic beverages to be served or sold at the event are purchased from a licensed wholesaler or donated pursuant to this Code section.
(9) If the event is a beer or wine tasting, then the event shall also be subject to the provisions of section 4-165.
(10) If a designee has been appointed by the Grady Cultural Center, Zebulon, or Grady County Museum and History Center for alcoholic beverage services for consumption on the premises, then only the designee shall submit an application for a special temporary event permit to be held at these locations.
(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19; Ord. No. 842, § 3, 7-11-22)

223:
(a) A city sanctioned or sponsored special alcohol event is one (1) that is held on designated city property, which may include streets and rights-of-way, located in the city's designated special entertainment districts, that is organized and sponsored by the City of Cairo or an affiliate board or authority, such as the downtown development authority (DDA), consistent with the provisions of section 4-160 where alcohol is sold and consumed.
(b) During city-sponsored special events allowing alcoholic beverages, members of the public shall be authorized to purchase, possess, and consume alcoholic beverages within a designated special event area subject to distance requirements for alcohol sales as outlined in this chapter and any law regulating the time for selling such beverages.

224:
(a) A special event use permit may be issued for the sale of alcoholic beverage for certain events which would otherwise require a retail dealer's license. (a) As used in this section, "open container" means any container, containing alcoholic beverages, which is immediately capable of being consumed from or the seal of which has been broken.

226:
(a) Any licensed alcoholic beverage caterer who additionally holds a valid license which authorizes the licensee to sell alcohol for consumption on the premises, or by the package for consumption off the premises, may be issued an off-premises license which authorizes such licensed alcoholic beverage caterer to sell alcohol by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function. Only a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer may distribute or sell alcoholic beverages by the drink at an authorized catered event, after the approval of a catered event permit application which has been signed by the caterer and the host or sponsor, as well as the owner of the venue or the owner's authorized agent if the host or sponsor is not the owner of the venue, giving their consent to the distribution of alcoholic beverages at that location. Such vehicle shall be marked only with the state license number with lettering that shall be two (2) inches high and one (1) inch wide on each side of the vehicle. No other wording or advertisement of the business shall be allowed.

(f) No licensed alcoholic beverage caterer shall employ any person under twenty-one (21) years of age to dispense, serve, sell or handle alcoholic beverages at authorized catered functions.
(g) No catered event permit will be issued for an event to be held at any location with respect to which any alcohol license has been denied or revoked within the past twelve (12) months.

(Ord. No. 810, § 1, 2-11-19)
227:
(a) A license shall be required for a "tasting room" location set up as a retail business for the tasting and selling of malt beverages and wine, and all the restrictions provided in this Code shall also apply.
(b) A request to conduct a special malt beverage or wine tasting event may be approved by the city council when such request is made in writing on an application furnished by the city clerk, and a non-refundable permit fee is submitted as set forth in section 4-12. (a) Home brewed malt beverages for purposes of this section shall be limited to malt beverages produced by an individual(s) pursuant to the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 3-5-4 and any applicable rules and regulations of the Georgia Department of Revenue.

For purposes of this article, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively attributed to them in this section.
Abandoned animal. A domesticated animal which has been placed or found upon private or public property or roadways without the permission of the owner, tenant, or custodian of the property thereof, and left unattended and uncared for upon such property. An animal shall also be considered abandoned if it is retained upon the property of the owner or custodian without food and water for a period exceeding thirty-six (36) hours.
Animal control officer. Any person designated by the mayor and council to enforce the provisions of this article.
Animal control shelter. The facility designated by the mayor and council and/or any governmental unit with whom the city may have a contract for the detention or impoundment of animals.
City is the City of Cairo, a municipality and the entire area embraced in the corporate limits of the City of Cairo, Georgia.
Domesticated animal. An animal that is accustomed to live in and about the habitation of the population, including but not limited to fowl, cats, dogs, cows, horses, swine, sheep, and goats.
Guard dog. A dog which has been trained to attack persons or other animals independently or upon command or any dog, while not so trained, which reasonably is expected to perform as a guardian of the property upon which he or she is located.
Humane manner. Care of a domestic animal to include, but not be limited to, adequate heat, ventilation and sanitary shelter, or manner of restraint, wholesome food and water, consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, species, and breed.
Owner. Any person, firm, corporation, organization or department possessing, harboring or having the care or custody whether temporarily or permanently of a domesticated animal for a period of seventy-two (72) hours or more.
Restraint. An animal is "under restraint" within the meaning of this article if it is (1) controlled by a leash, (2) at "heel" or accompanying a competent person and obedient to that person's commands (under verbal control of owner or other person), (3) on or within a vehicle driven or parked on the streets, and (4) within the property limits of its owner.
Untagged animal. An animal is considered to be untagged if a valid license tag is not attached to a collar which is kept on the animal.
Vicious animals. Any animal which constitutes a physical threat to human beings or other domesticated or wild animals by virtue of attacking or biting a person or other animal without provocation shall be deemed a vicious animal. This definition shall not be deemed to include any activity which is permitted under the game laws of the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 402, § 1, 6-10-91; Ord. No. 653, § 1, 2-14-07)

(Ord. No. 402, § 1, 6-10-91)
252:
It shall be unlawful for any person to permit an animal under his ownership, possession, control or care to be a nuisance as defined herein or under restraint as set forth within this article within the city. An animal shall be deemed to be a nuisance for the following reasons:
(1) Lack of proof of current rabies vaccination.
(2) Biting of person or animal.
(3) Upon request by law enforcement agency or health department following investigation and determination that an animal is a nuisance or vicious as defined herein.
Except for a person in an occupation requiring or involving the keeping of animals located within areas permitted by City of Cairo zoning regulations, no person shall be allowed to keep more than four (4) animals at any location. Puppies and kittens less than ten (10) weeks shall be excluded.

253:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation, organization or department to possess or maintain within the city any animal that is vicious unless such animal is confined and secured upon the property of the owner or other person having custody of such animal in such a manner as would prohibit such animal from molesting, attacking or biting any person or other animal. Such animal shall be securely confined indoors or in a securely enclosed and locked pen or structure suitable to prevent the injury of young children, and designed to prevent the animal from escaping. Such pen or structure must have a minimum dimension of five (5) feet by ten (10) feet and must have secure sides and a secure top. If it has no bottom secured to the sides, the sides must be embedded into the ground no less than two (2) feet. The enclosure must also provide protection from the elements for the animal.
The owner or keeper shall display a sign on his or her premises facing out from all sides of the premises warning that there is a dangerous animal on the property. This sign should be visible and capable of being read from a public highway or thoroughfare within twenty (20) feet of its placement.
A vicious animal may be off the owner's premises only if it is muzzled and restrained by an approved lead or chain not exceeding three (3) feet in length and is under the control of an adult who is an able-bodied person. The muzzle must be made in a manner that will not cause injury to the animal or interfere with its vision or respiration but must prevent it from biting any person or animal.

Further, the owner, tenant or custodian shall post the universal symbol for guard/dangerous dog in a prominent and conspicuous location on such property. Identification. Any person owning a vicious animal shall on or before April 1, 2007 and annually thereafter on or before April 1 of each year register that animal and provide a current color photograph of that animal with the office of clerk of the city and pay a registration fee in the amount of forty dollars ($40.00). It shall be unlawful for any person to hinder, interfere, harass or otherwise obstruct the performance of any officer of the animal control division in the official performance of the duties as provided in this article.
(Ord. No. 402, § 1, 6-10-91)
265:
Any person who violates the provisions of this article shall be issued a citation for that violation to appear in the municipal court of the city. The citation may be issued by a police officer or by a magistrate upon receiving the sworn statement of a designated animal control officer based upon his own personal knowledge or upon a sworn written statement of another person who witnessed the violation, in which case the animal control officer and/or witness shall be subpoenaed to testify for the city in municipal court.
Any person convicted of a violation of this article shall be punished in accordance with section 1-8 of the Code of Ordinances of the city.
(Ord. No. 402, § 1, 6-10-91)
390:

State Law reference— Municipal corporations as trustees for cemeteries, OCGA § 36-37-4 et seq.
392:
No person shall dig, or cause to be dug, or direct or permit or allow to be dug any grave in a city cemetery upon any lot owned or controlled by such person without first obtaining a permit from the cemetery supervisor or such other person as may be authorized by the city manager showing the exact location of such grave. The city shall mark the four (4) corners of the grave space. Upon request by the funeral director, the city shall mark the location of interment but the city assumes no responsibility for ascertaining the proper location.
(Code 1965, § 8-3; Ord. No. 421, § 1, 11-23-92; Ord. No. 515, 2-8-99)
393:
No person shall erect, place or cause to be erected or placed any monument or tombstone or any curbing or coping in any city cemetery without first obtaining a permit to do so from the cemetery supervisor or such other person as may be authorized by the city manager showing the exact location thereof.
(Code 1965, § 8-5; Ord. No. 421, § 2, 11-23-92)
394:
No person shall dig, or direct or instruct any person to dig any grave in any city cemetery of the city in any walkway, driveway or passageway, or erect any tombstone, monument, curbing or coping in any of the walkways, driveways, or passageways of the cemetery.
(Code 1965, § 8-4)
395:
No person shall walk across or use as a walkway any part of any cemetery grounds in the city except the regular driveways, within the cemetery or except on regularly designated and established walkways between the private burial lots in the cemetery, nor shall any person park a vehicle thereon.
(Code 1965, § 8-1)
396:
All interments hereafter made shall be in outer burial containers, sometimes called vaults, of concrete or stronger substance (such as stainless steel). The vault shall not be required for an indigent burial. (Indigence to be certified by Georgia Department of Family and Children Services.) The city will allow the use of a box in lieu of a vault.
(Ord No. 515, 2-8-99)
397:
The city clerk shall handle all sales of cemetery lots and shall be the custodian of the master maps or plats of cemeteries located within the city.
(Ord. No. 397, § 2, 4-22-91)
398:
Cemetery lots located within the city shall be sold at the prices established by the governing body.
(Ord. No. 397, § 2, 4-22-91)
399:
(a) No conveyance after the initial purchase of a lot in any cemetery shall be made without approval of the city.
(b) The charge of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for each conveyance and legal and recording fees that may be incurred by the city shall be charged to the purchaser and collected by the city.
(c) There will be no swapping of cemetery lots within the city owned cemeteries. If so desired after the purchase of a lot the purchaser may resell the lot to a third party at which time there will be an administrative fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) and any associated legal and recording fees.
(Ord. No. 397, § 2, 4-22-91; Ord. No. 585, § 1, 12-9-02)
400:
Cemetery lots shall be sold without regard to residency of purchases as follows:
Cemetery | Cost per grave space
Cairo | $300.00
Crestview | $300.00
Greenwood | $300.00
Forest Lawn | $300.00
(Ord. No. 599 § 1, 10-13-03; Ord. No. 659, § 1, 4-9-07; Ord. No. 760, § 1, 9-9-14; Ord. of 07-01-22(1))
401:
The following regulations shall apply to all city owned cemeteries:
(1) There shall be a minimum of eighteen (18) inches of ground cover over each vault.
(2) All graves should be water packed if buried underground.
(3) All excavation material shall be removed from the cemetery lot and placed at a location designated by the city.
(4) Two (2) infant burials may occur on the same lot if vaults total less than eight (8) feet in length.
(5) Any child vault over four (4) feet in length shall be buried in one (1) grave space.
(6) There will be a record fee charge for each grave space or lot sold in any cemetery.
(7) Upon the following conditions, the city shall permit up to six (6) infants to be buried within a lot:
a. The casket shall be less than two (2) feet in length.
b. The Department of Family and Children Services shall certify the parents of the infant to be indigent.
c. The city shall permit the use of a box in lieu of a vault.
(8) There shall be a maximum of two (2) cremation burials in each grave space.
(9) All vaults shall be properly sealed.
(10) All cemeteries shall be open to the public from sunrise until sunset daily.
(Ord. No. 617, § 1, 7-12-04; Ord. No. 628, § 1, 8-22-04; Ord. No. 638, § 1, 4-10-06; Ord. No. 639, § 1, 5-8-06)
402:
Grave sites may be decorated in a manner that is not generally offensive to public taste in such manner as interested parties desire. Such adornment or decoration shall be within the grave site area and shall in no manner obstruct or interfere with the maintenance of the cemetery. Adornment or decoration shall be the sole responsibility of the person or entity placing same. Such decoration or adornment may be removed by the City of Cairo if same shall be offensive, or interfere with the maintenance of the cemetery. The City of Cairo shall have no liability regarding the damage or destruction of grave adornment or decoration unless the City of Cairo shall have intentionally or by gross negligence damaged or destroyed the adornment or decoration.
(Ord. No. 696, § 1, 6-26-08)
405:
The cemetery located on the Thomasville-Cairo Highway lying in the northeastern section of the city, is hereby designated as Greenwood Cemetery, and Crestview Cemetery is located adjacent to and north of Greenwood Cemetery.
(Code 1965, § 8-11)
406:
No coping, fence, hedge, planting, wall, ditch, bank, or enclosure of any kind or nature shall be placed, planted or used or have the appearance of being used for outlining, enclosing, marking off or making or designating any boundary line of any lot or plot in Greenwood Cemetery or Crestview Cemetery, except six-inch square white marble or concrete markers to mark the four (4) corners of any lot. The markers shall be flush with the ground and set within the boundaries of the lot.
(Code 1965, § 8-15; Ord. No. 397, § 3, 4-22-91)

No. 397, § 1, adopted Apr. 22, 1991 amended the Code by deleting former §§ 7-21—7-23, which pertained to supervision of sales of lots and the custodian of the cemetery plat, cost of lots, and approval of conveyances, respectively, and derived from the 1965 Code, §§ 8-12—8-14. 407:
No tombstone, marker, monument, slab or memorial shall be more than thirty-six (36) inches in height unless same shall be in the form of a mausoleum. Design of such mausoleum shall be brought before mayor and council for approval. Upon approval, such mausoleum shall be constructed within no less than eighteen (18) months.
(Code 1965, § 8-16; Ord. No. 397, § 3, 4-22-91; Ord. No. 658, § 1, 4-9-07)
Note— See the editor's note following § 7-21.
408:
The provisions of this article pertaining to use of lots shall be incorporated in and made a part of the deed of conveyance to any lot or plot in Greenwood Cemetery or Crestview Cemetery.
(Code 1965, § 8-17; Ord. No. 397, § 3, 4-22-91)
Note— See the editor's note following § 7-21.
411:
The cemetery located on 11th Avenue, N.W. is hereby designated as Forest Lawn Cemetery.
(Ord. No. 397, § 4, 4-22-91)
412:
No lot shall be transferred from one party to another without approval of the city. No coping, fence, hedge, planting, wall, ditch, bank or enclosure of any kind or nature shall be placed, planted or used or have the appearance of being used for outlining, enclosing, marking off or making or designating any boundary line of any lot or plot in said cemetery. No burial vaults shall be permitted above ground level. All burial vaults shall use some type of concrete vault. All vaults must be buried eighteen (18) inches beneath the top soil. No lots shall be permitted with cement or rocks around monuments. No concrete slabs or ledgers shall be placed on grave. No monument shall exceed seventy-two (72) inches in height.
(Ord. No. 397, § 5, 4-22-91)
413:
The provisions of this article pertaining to use of lots shall be incorporated in and made a part of the deed of conveyance to any lot or plot in Forest Lawn Cemetery.
(Ord. No. 397, § 6, 4-22-91)
414:
Grave spaces shall be sold only in one (1) section until such time as all grave spaces within that section have been sold.
(Ord. No. 515, 2-8-99; Ord. No. 617, § 1, 7-12-04)
415:
(a) All crypts (mausoleums) shall be made of marble or granite. No concrete crypts shall be allowed.
(b) Crypts shall be no more than thirty-six (36) inches in height.
(c) All crypts must have concrete foundation and a blue print showing foundation requirements as follows:
(1) Concrete shall have no less than three thousand (3,000) PSI.
(2) Concrete shall be at least one (1) foot deep.
(3) Concrete shall contain one (1) inch re-bar six (6) inches up from ground level.
(4) Rock of number seven (7) size must be six (6) inches deep for drainage as specified in blue print.
(5) All crypts must face east and west.
(Ord. No. 515, 2-8-99; Ord. No. 528, § 1, 6-13-2000; Ord. No. 617, § 2, 7-12-04)
416:
The city may construct, shall maintain, and does establish the following rules and guidelines regarding any columbarium located in Forest Lawn Cemetery:
(1) Transfer of ownership will only be allowed with written confirmation of the City of Cairo.
(2) The City of Cairo shall be solely responsible for the upkeep of the columbarium. The City of Cairo is not responsible or liable for theft or damage to the contents of the columbarium.
(3) Possession of the key to unlock each burial niche within the columbarium will be held by the City of Cairo. The provisions regarding the use of a niche shall be incorporated within the document transferring title to the niche.
(4) The document relating to transfer of a burial niche shall be as prescribed by the City of Cairo.
(5) A burial niche may only be unlocked or opened for interring cremains or upon the permanent removal of cremains before sealing. Following sealing of a niche, a niche may not be reopened. Any necessary reopening of a niche will require payment of a fee established by mayor and council.
(6) All burial niches must be marked when cremains are interred. All markings shall be done through the City of Cairo in such manner as the City of Cairo shall prescribe.
(7) The cost of a burial niche shall be five hundred dollars ($500.00) and each sealing and marking of a niche as permitted shall result in a fee of three hundred dollars ($300.00).
(Ord. No. 765, § 1, 3-23-15)
418:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Recorder's court, OCGA § 36-32-1 et seq.
419:
(a) There is hereby established a court to be known as the "Municipal Court, City of Cairo," which shall have jurisdiction and authority to try offenses against laws and ordinances of said city and to punish for a violation of the same.
(b) Such court shall have the power to enforce its judgments by the imposition of such penalties as may be provided by law; to punish witnesses for nonattendance, and to punish also any person who may counsel or advise, aid, encourage, or persuade another whose testimony is desired or material in any proceeding before said court, to go or move beyond the reach of the process of the court; to try all offenses within the territorial limits of the city constituting traffic cases which under the laws of the state are placed within the jurisdiction of municipal or police courts to the extent of and in accordance with the provisions of such laws and all laws subsequently enacted amendatory thereof; to establish bail and recognizances to insure the presence of those charged with violations and to prescribe the conditions of forfeiture of the same; and to administer oaths and to perform all other acts necessary and proper to the conduct of said court.
(c) The presiding officer of the court is the municipal judge who shall be known as judge of said court.
(d) Said court shall be convened at such times as designated in this chapter or at such times as deemed necessary to keep current the dockets thereof.
(e) The court shall sit at a place designated by the governing body.
(Ord. No. 255, § 2, 6-29-82)
420:
(a) No person shall be qualified or eligible to serve as municipal judge unless such person shall have attained the age of twenty-one (21) years, shall not have been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude and shall be qualified to vote in this county. Until such time that the governing body shall appoint a judge, the mayor, or in the mayor's absence the mayor pro tem shall act as judge. The compensation of the judge shall be fixed by the governing body.
(b) The judge may appoint a judge pro hac vice to serve in the absence of the judge. Said judge pro hac vice shall have the same qualifications as the judge and shall be known as associate judge of said court.
(c) Before entering on duties of office, the judge shall take an oath before an officer duly authorized to administer oaths in this state, that such judge will truly, honestly and faithfully, discharge the duties of the office to the best of such judge's ability without fear, favor, or partiality. This oath shall be entered upon the minutes of the meeting of the governing body.
(Ord. No. 255, § 2, 6-29-82)
421:
(a) The judge shall have power to impose fines, costs and forfeitures for the violation of any law or ordinance of the city.
(b) Said municipal court is hereby empowered to punish violators of the rules, regulations, and ordinances of the city and may fix punishment for offenses within its jurisdiction being a fine in such amount as is permitted by state law or imprisonment for such time as is permitted by state law, or any combination of the two. Said fines may be collected by execution issued against all property of the defendant, both real and personal, if any to be found.
(c) Said judge shall have the authority to punish for contempt by imposing a fine of two hundred dollars ($200.00) or imprisonment not exceeding thirty (30) days, or any combination of the two (2). The judge shall be, to all intents and purposes, a justice of the peace, so far as to enable such judge to issue warrants for offenses committed within the limits of the city, and to commit the offenders to jail or admit them to bail in bailable cases for their appearance at a regularly scheduled term of court of competent jurisdiction to be held in the city.
(d) The court shall also have concurrent jurisdiction with that of a justice of the peace over offenses against the criminal laws of the state committed within the corporate limits.
(e) Except as may be herein otherwise specified, the court is specifically invested with all jurisdiction and powers throughout the entire area within the corporate limits granted by state laws generally to mayors, municipal, recorders', and police courts, and particularly such laws as authorize the abatement of nuisances.
(f) Said judge is hereby authorized to administer oaths.
(Ord. No. 255, § 2, 6-29-82; Ord. No. 683, § 1, 4-28-08; Ord. No. 782, § 1, 4-25-16)
Editor's note— Pursuant to instructions from the city, the fine of "six hundred dollars ($600.00)" in subsection (b) of § 9-3 has been changed to read "one thousand dollars ($1,000.00)," thereby reflecting the maximum amount of fine as set forth in § 8 of Art. No. 275 of the 1985 General Assembly.
422:
The right of appeal and procedures pertaining to appeal bonds to the superior court from the municipal court shall lie in the same manner under the same procedure as generally prescribed for appeals and appeal bonds from the court of probate. An appeal to the superior court shall be a de novo proceeding, and the city shall be entitled to reimbursement of its costs therefor.
(Ord. No. 255, § 2, 6-29-82)
423:
(a) In all cases in the municipal court, the costs incurred and allowable herein may be computed under the provisions of the laws of the state fixing costs in the justice of the peace courts of said state, or the governing body may establish a schedule of fees to defray costs of operation and the city shall be entitled to reimbursement of the costs, meals, transportation and caretaking of prisoners bound over to the superior court for violations of state law.
(b) The governing body may also provide a uniform scale of costs of the clerk and police officers of said city for all services in the arrest and prosecution of offenders in the municipal court and in the issuance and collection of tax and other executions; and for their collections and payment into the city treasury.
(c) The judge is hereby authorized to issue subpoenas to compel the attendance of witnesses to said court and to issue such other processes as may be necessary for the proper administration of said court.
(Ord. No. 255, § 2, 6-29-82)
424:
Sessions of the municipal court shall be convened at regular intervals and held on dates and times as set by the municipal court judge and may continue from hour to hour or day to day as the business of the court may necessitate, provided, any session may be dispensed with when there is no business pending in the court and no case ready for trial.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82; Ord. No. 683, § 2, 4-28-08)
425:
(a) The judge may hold special sessions when it is determined by the judge to be necessary or there is urgent cause for the trial of accused persons, before the next regular sitting of the court. The necessity or urgency of the cause shall be presumed from the fact of a session being held.
(b) All defendants shall have at least six (6) hours notice of the session.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
426:
(a) Practice in the municipal court shall be governed by the rules of the superior courts of this state as far as practicable, under the ordinances and charter of the city, and, where not provided otherwise by the charter and ordinances of the city, the court may prescribe additional rules of practice where there are no rules applicable.
(b) The judge shall have the powers of a superior court judge to control the proceedings in said court.
(Ord. No. 255, §§ 2, 3, 6-29-82)
427:
(a) It shall be the duty of the chief of police or the chief's assistant or some member of the police force designated by the judge to attend each session of the court to act as bailiff, and the duty of each police officer making the arrest or having knowledge of the case for or against the defendant, to attend the trial of any person brought before the court.
(b) Any police officer who is off duty during the hours that the court is in session and has been specifically notified to be present in court as a witness by the chief of police, judge, or court clerk shall be present at the appointed date and time.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82; Ord. No. 683, § 3, 4-28-08)
428:
(a) It shall be the duty of the city clerk, or an appropriate designee of the governing body, to attend each session of the municipal court and serve as clerk of court.
(b) The clerk of court shall:
(1) Prepare all subpoenas and warrants and maintain a docket thereof that will show the name of the person for whom the subpoena or warrant was issued, its date, at whose instance it was issued, and to whom delivered.
(2) The judge may require that the clerk maintain a duplicate court docket and use the signed duplicate copy of the docket to make necessary entries in the master docket after each session of court, the master or original to be retained by the judge and the duplicate to be examined for completeness and signed by the judge.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
429:
Every person arrested by a police officer of the city shall be held in custody by the arresting officer by and for the city, pending disposition as provided in this chapter.
(Code 1965, § 26-18(1))
430:
(a) All charges cognizable as violations of state laws shall be handled by a commitment hearing, provided however, that they may be adjudicated in the municipal court whenever the court would have jurisdiction over the offense, and the defendant does not demand a jury trial.
(b) When a defendant is bound over to the appropriate state court, such defendant may be released under any of the following methods:
(1) If the defendant has made bond to the city such defendant may be released on the same bond.
(2) If the defendant has not made bond before being bound over, such defendant shall make bond at the county jail book-in and arraignment notice will then be given to the defendant and the defendant must be delivered, in person, by the city police, to the county authorities.
(c) There shall be no jury trials in the municipal court; where one is required by law or where one is rightfully demanded, said case shall be bound over to the appropriate court by the municipal judge.
(Code 1965, § 26-21; Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
431:
Offenses against the ordinances of the city shall be bailable as follows:
(1) The arresting officer, chief of police, recorder or any other officer designated by the chief of police, may accept bond of the accused payable to the city conditioned upon the appearance of the accused at the next session or any subsequent session of the municipal court as stated in the bond, to answer the charge.
(2) The bond shall be in writing in an amount established in a schedule approved by the recorder.
(3) A person arrested for violation of a city ordinance may be released on such person's recognizance, may be released on bond without security or in lieu thereof may deposit cash or such person's driver's license with the arresting officer.
(4) Any person released under subsection (3) above shall receive a receipt for any driver's license deposited or, if released on the person's own recognizance, shall sign and receive a copy of the citation or ticket describing the violation for which the person was arrested.
(5) All persons arrested or notified by citation or ticket of parking violations shall be released on their own recognizance.
(Code 1965, § 26-19; Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
432:
(a) The municipal judge or the judge's designee shall call the case in its regular order, and, if the accused is not in court and does not answer the call, and, if no good and sufficient reason is given for nonappearance, the judge shall enter on the docket where the case is stated "Bond forfeited," or similar words.
(b) Upon forfeiture of any bond, the cash deposited as security shall be paid to the city clerk, and it shall become the property of the city.
(c) Upon the forfeiture of any bond signed by a person as surety, the city clerk shall issue an execution against the principal and surety on the bond for the amount thereof which shall be collected as tax executions are collected.
(Code 1965, § 26-20; Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
433:
(a) Upon a case being called, the municipal judge shall inform the defendant of the charge against such defendant and shall inquire as to how such defendant desires to plead thereon. Thereupon, the defendant shall enter one of the following pleas:
(1) Guilty;
(2) Not guilty;
(3) Nolo contendere (with the permission of the court); or
(4) A former judgment of conviction or acquittal of the offense charged.
(b) If the defendant refuses to enter a plea, the court shall enter a plea of not guilty and set the case down for trial.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
434:
The municipal judge may refuse to continue a case, except for good cause shown.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
435:
A material or complaining witness in any contested prosecution shall appear at the session at which the prosecution is docketed. The prosecution may be dismissed if the material witness fails to appear.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
437:
(a) For fines that may be due by any defendant, execution may be issued by the city clerk and collected as tax executions are collected.
(b) Persons charged with traffic violations may, prior to the time for their court appearance, plead guilty in writing and pay to the city as their fine the amount set as the appearance bond for the offense charged; except that those persons charged with driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs and those charged with an offense in connection with an automobile collision shall be required in all cases to appear before the court for disposition of the case.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
438:
Failure to appear pursuant to any summons or subpoena, disrespectful conduct or failure to comply with any other order or judgment of the court shall constitute contempt of court and be punishable as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
439:
(a) Court date will be made known to the defendant at the time of the arrest process and shall be properly indicated on the copy of charges given to the defendant by the arresting officer.
(b) Warrants for contempt of court charges may be issued following each session of court.
(c) Appeals may be taken from the municipal court in accordance with applicable state law.
(Ord. No. 255, § 3, 6-29-82)
440:
Footnote 1:
Cross reference— Occupational license taxes, Ch. 14.
442:
(a) The fiscal year of the city shall begin on the first day of July and end on the thirtieth day of June.
(b) The fiscal year shall constitute the budget year of the city.
(Code 1965, § 11-12)
445:
(a) The budget of the city shall present a complete financial plan for the ensuing budget year.
(b) The budget shall set forth:
(1) All proposed expenditures for the administration, operation and maintenance of all offices, departments, boards, commissions and activities, including publicly owned and operated utilities and enterprises.
(2) The actual or estimated operating deficits from prior years.
(3) All interest and debt redemption charges during the budget year.
(4) Expenditures for capital projects to be undertaken or executed during the budget year, including expenditures for local improvements which may be paid for in whole or in part by special assessments.
(5) The anticipated income and other means of financing the proposed expenditures for the fiscal year.
(Code 1965, § 11-13)
446:
The budget document shall consist of three (3) parts, the nature and contents of which shall be as follows:
(1) Part I shall consist of a budget message prepared by the city manager which shall outline the fiscal policy of the city for the fiscal year, describing in connection therewith the important features of the budget plan; it shall also embrace a general budget summary setting forth the aggregate figures of the budget in such manner as to show the balanced relations between the total proposed expenditures and the total anticipated income and other means of financing the budget for the ensuing fiscal year, contrasted with the corresponding figures for the last completed fiscal year and the year in progress. The general budget summary shall be supported by explanatory schedules or statements, classifying the expenditures contained therein by organization units, sources and funds.
(2) Part II shall contain the detailed budget estimates both of expenditures and revenues as provided for in section 10-20. It shall also include statements of the bonded indebtedness of the city showing the debt redemption requirements, the debt authorized and unissued, the condition of any sinking funds, and the borrowing capacity; in addition thereto, it shall contain any statements relative to the financial plan which the city manager may deem desirable or which may be required by the governing body.
(3) Part III shall contain complete drafts of the budget ordinances; that is, the ordinances required to give legal sanction to the financial plan when adopted by the governing body. These ordinances shall include an appropriation ordinance, authorizing by spending agencies and funds, all expenditures of the city for budget year; and such other ordinances as may be required to provide the income necessary to finance the budget.
(Code 1965, § 11-14)
447:
At least sixty (60) days prior to the beginning of the fiscal year, all departments, offices, boards and other spending agencies of the city shall prepare and submit to the city manager estimates of their expenditure requirements and their estimated revenues for the forthcoming budget year, compared with the corresponding figures of the last completed fiscal year and the estimated figures for the year in progress. The expenditure estimates shall be classified to set forth the data by funds, organizations, units, character, and objects of expenditure; the organization units may be subclassified by functions and activities at the discretion of the city manager. The revenue estimates shall be classified so as to show the receipts by funds, organization units and sources of income.
(1) The city manager shall review the estimates, altering, revising, increasing or decreasing the items of such estimates as such officer shall deem necessary in view of the needs of the various spending agencies and the probable income of the city. The city manager shall then prepare a budget in the form required by the provisions of section 10-21.
(2) The city manager shall transmit the budget to the governing body at least thirty (30) days before the beginning of the fiscal year.
(Code 1965, § 11-15)
Cross reference— Budget year, § 10-1.
448:
(a) Final action shall not be taken on the proposed budget until at least one public hearing has been held thereon after ten (10) days' notice thereof.
(b) The governing body shall arrange for and hold such hearing.
(c) The budget, when submitted by the city manager to the governing body, shall be published, advertised or otherwise made available for public inspection at least ten (10) days prior to the date set for the hearing.
(Code 1965, § 11-16)
449:
At least one (1) week after the conclusion of the hearing required in section 10-23, the governing body shall consider the budget as submitted to it by the city manager and shall adopt a budget ordinance making appropriations in such sums as the governing authority may deem sufficient, whether greater or less than the sums presented in the proposed budget. The budget ordinance shall be adopted at a public meeting which shall be advertised at least one week prior to the meeting.
(Code 1965, § 11-17; Ord. No. 718, § 1, 6-14-10)
Editor's note— Section 1 of Ord. No. 718, adopted June 14, 2010, changed the title of § 10-24 from "Adoption; publication of budget summary after adoption" to "Adoption of budget ordinance."
450:
(a) The appropriation ordinance, provided for in section 10-21, shall be drawn in such form as to authorize only lump sum appropriations to meet the expenditure needs of the various spending agencies of the municipal government.
(b) For the operation and maintenance expenses of each department, office, board or other spending agency, there shall be a single appropriation, which shall be allotted as provided in section 10-29 before becoming available for expenditure.
(c) Appropriations for the acquisition of property shall be in such detail under each spending agency as the city manager shall determine; provided, however, that such appropriations shall not be segregated into greater detail than the major classes, or projects, for which they are expendable.
(Code 1965, § 11-18)
451:
If at the termination of any fiscal year, the appropriations necessary for the support of the municipal government of the city for the ensuing fiscal year shall not have been made, the several amounts appropriated in the last appropriation ordinance for the objects and purposes therein specified, so far as the same shall relate to the operation and maintenance expenses, shall be deemed to be reappropriated for the several objects and purposes specified in the last appropriation ordinance; and until the governing body shall act in such behalf, the treasurer shall make the payments necessary for the support of the municipal government on the basis of the appropriations of the preceding fiscal year.
(Code 1965, § 11-19)
452:
The governing body may, during a fiscal year, make additional appropriations or increase existing appropriations to meet emergencies. Such work program shall show the requested allotments and appropriations for such spending agency by months for the entire year.
(b) The city manager shall review the requested allotments in the light of the work program of the spending agency concerned, and shall, if deemed necessary, revise, alter or change such allotments before approving them.
(c) The aggregate of such allotments shall not exceed the total appropriations available to the spending agency for the budget year.
(d) The city manager shall transmit copies of the approved allotments to the head of the spending agency concerned and to the city treasurer.
(e) The treasurer shall authorize all expenditures to be made from the appropriations on the basis of such allotments, and not otherwise.
(f) The head of any spending agency of the municipal government, whenever such head shall deem it necessary by reason of changed conditions, may revise the work program of such person's agency at the beginning of any month during the budget year and submit such revised program to the city manager with a request for a revision of the allotments for the remaining months of the budget year. If, upon a re-examination of the work program, the city manager shall grant the request for a revision of the allotments, the same procedure, so far as it relates to review, approval and control, shall be followed as in making the original allotments.

(a) The only type of fires permitted for the purpose of land clearing is pit fires. Nonpit fires are not permitted for land clearing within the city limits. All pit fires shall be conducted in strict accordance with the "Air Curtain Destructor Operating Guide and Procedures," as published by the Environmental Protection Division.
(b) Pit fires shall comply with the following stipulations:
(1) The pit shall be at least three hundred (300) feet from any occupied or habitable structure. This distance may be decreased upon determination by the fire department.
(2) Where a site cannot be excavated to the recommended depth due to high water table and/or subsurface rock, the pit may be constructed above ground level, subject to the same state standards and procedures for a pit below ground level.
(3) Only wood wastes consisting of trees, logs, large brush, stumps, leaves, and untreated lumber may be burned in the pit.
(4) Leaves, sawdust or other densely packed wood wastes, paper (any type), chemically treated, coated or impregnated wood, or nonwood construction materials shall not be burned. The amount of dirt/soil mixture shall be kept to a minimum.
(5) No more than one (1) air curtain destructor is allowed to be operated within a ten-acre permitted site at one (1) time. The air curtain destructor must be under the supervision of a trained operator at all times during operation. If there is a need for multiple burning pits, there shall be a minimum of one thousand (1,000) feet between each burning pit.
(6) Air curtain destructors shall be able to pass an even, nonturbulent flow of air across the top of the pit. Air curtain destructors with an air duct or manifold that has been altered by bends, dents, holes, etc., and are incapable of providing an even and nonturbulent flow of air across the top of the pit shall not be approved for use.
(7) The air curtain destructor shall be operated in a manner to prevent air, land or water pollution, safety/health hazards or nuisances.
(8) Tires or other rubber products, plastics, heavy oils or asphaltic base or impregnated materials shall not be used to start or maintain air curtain destructor operations.
(9) When the pit is cleared of ash, airborne particulate is to be minimized by wetting or mixing the ashes with dirt.
(10) Diesel fuel or kerosene only may be used to start pit fires.
(Ord. No. 749, § 3, 10-14-13)
